findings.description: Method syncUnsyncedDocuments() has return type Future<void> but contains 'return null;'
findings.impact: Build-breaking compilation error prevents application from compiling
findings.correction: Change 'return null;' to 'return;' for Future<void> method
findings.user_consequence: Application will not build or deploy

findings.description: Misplaced 'if (!context.mounted) return;' statement inside Theme constructor parameters
findings.evidence: builder: (context, child) { return Theme( if (!context.mounted) return; data: Theme.of(context).copyWith(...), child: child!, ); }
findings.impact: 8 compilation errors (missing_required_argument, missing_identifier, expected_token) - appears in 2 locations
findings.correction: Move context.mounted check before the Theme constructor: if (!context.mounted) return const SizedBox.shrink();
findings.user_consequence: Application will not compile. Date picker widget will fail to render.

findings.description: Multiple return type mismatches in async methods
findings.evidence: Line 326: return_without_value; Line 367: returning null in Future<List<Learner>>; Lines 605,614: returning bool in Future<void>
findings.correction: Line 326: Add explicit return value; Line 367: Return empty list or throw; Lines 605,614,665: Change 'return false;' to 'return;'
findings.user_consequence: Application will not compile. Learner sync and database operations will fail.

findings.description: Direct SQL interpolation without prepared statements
findings.evidence: $learnerId = isset($_GET['learner_id']) ? intval($_GET['learner_id']) : 0; $result = $conn->query("SELECT * FROM learnerdetails WHERE LearnerID = $learnerId");
findings.impact: SQL injection vulnerability - inconsistent with rest of codebase which uses prepared statements
findings.correction: Use prepared statements: $stmt = $conn->prepare("SELECT * FROM learnerdetails WHERE LearnerID = ?"); $stmt->bind_param("i", $learnerId);
findings.user_consequence: Potential security vulnerability if exploited. However, intval() provides partial protection and this appears to be a debug script.
findings.note: Most other PHP APIs correctly use prepared statements. This may be a diagnostic tool not in production.
